short: After nearly nineteen years in English captivity, Mary, Queen of Scots, was beheaded for her complicity in the Babington Plot.
full:
Following the exposure of the Babington Plot in 1586, Mary, Queen of Scots, was brought to trial before an English court. The intercepted letters proved her explicit endorsement of the conspiracy to assassinate Elizabeth I. Despite Mary's defence that she was a sovereign monarch not subject to English law, she was found guilty of treason and sentenced to death.

Elizabeth hesitated for months before signing the death warrant, fearing the precedent of executing an anointed queen and the potential backlash from Catholic Europe. When she finally signed it, her council dispatched the warrant immediately to prevent her from changing her mind. Mary was beheaded at Fotheringhay Castle on 8 February 1587. Her execution permanently eliminated a Catholic focus for rebellion in England but gave Philip II of Spain the justification he sought to launch the Spanish Armada.
